description: U.S. President Donald Trump clarified Sunday afternoon that he was "only kidding" about his offer for UFC CEO Dana White to fulfill the open role of White House press secretary. Speaking to reporters in West Palm Beach, Florida, Trump expressed surprise at the reaction to his announcement and insisted his proposal was never meant to be taken seriously. However, the president also claimed that White was enthusiastic about the idea and confirmed the two are expected to meet Monday in Washington, D.C. Trump said the meeting was previously scheduled and concerned unrelated matters. Trump's full comments Sunday: "You would've thought that people would've said, 'He's having a good time.' I will tell you, I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea. And there's only one Dana, he's great. I don't know, you wouldn't mess around with him so much. So I was kidding, of course. title: 8-year-old Haitian boy in federal custody after ICE check-in
author: LAURA ROMERO (ABC News)
categories: ABCN/US
description: An 8-year-old Haitian boy who lost Temporary Protected Status earlier this year was taken into federal custody after an immigration check-in, according to local advocates and school officials. The third grader, who attends Fay Elementary School in San Diego, was placed into government custody alone after attending an Immigration and Customs Enforcement appointment with his uncle on Thursday, according to his school district and an advocacy group. “The eight-year-old received a letter to meet with an ICE agent,” the San Diego Unified School District said in a letter to DHS. “His uncle, with whom he’s been living since the child’s father was deported more than a year ago, took him to meet the agent because he did not want to break the law.” New ICE facility to hold families, unaccompanied minors could open in Louisiana next week Advocates and school officials said the boy had been living with his uncle and cousins after his father was deported to Mexico last year. title: Trump says he was ‘only kidding’ about making UFC’s Dana White next press secretary
author: Robert Mackey
categories: Donald Trump | Trump administration | UFC | US news | Sport | US politics | Media | US press and publishing | US sports
description: President says it was ‘just a little fun’ to picture White, UFC boss and Trump’s friend, in briefing room with fighters Donald Trump said on Sunday that he “was only kidding” when he announced a day earlier that he had offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship ( UFC ). Speaking to reporters on his way back the White House from his beach club in Florida, Trump explained the premise of his joke, that if the UFC boss, who is a devoted fan of the president, took over the briefing room, flanked by six fighters, reporters “wouldn’t mess around with him so much”.

title: Teaching GCSE topics younger risks turning schools into ‘early exam factories’, Powell warns
author: Richard Adams Education editor
categories: National curriculum | Secondary schools | Schools | GCSEs | Exams | Education policy | Lucy Powell | Labour | Department for Education | Curriculums | Education | Politics | England | UK news
description: Lucy Powell says proposals to end widespread practice will be included in overhaul of England’s national curriculum Pushing GCSE subjects on younger pupils risks turning England’s secondary schools into “early exam factories”, the education secretary has said, warning that it is increasing disengagement from education. Lucy Powell wants schools to end the widespread practice of teaching GCSE topics to pupils in year 9 or earlier, before they officially start in year 10, and says she plans to reduce the amount of GCSE content to make it easier to fit into the official timetable.

title: In assessing GOP midterm losses, Trump says his supporters likely didn't vote
author: Ross Douthat (CBS News)
categories: 60Minutes
description: Days after Republicans faced a series of bruising midterm election losses, President Trump stood by his handling of the economy and the Iran war — but he acknowledged some "bad messaging" on economic issues and said his immigration crackdown was "too tough" at times. In a sitdown with 60 Minutes correspondent Ross Douthat, the president also suggested some top administration officials could be on their way out. One hour later, he announced White House chief of staff Susie Wiles would depart her role and be replaced by Stephen Miller. Here are the biggest takeaways from the interview: Why did Republicans lose? Republicans lost more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats on Tuesday, with some races still uncalled, including in places that Mr. Trump won by double-digit margins two years ago. title: Trump says his deportation policy ‘might have been too tough’ for voters in the election
author: Ross Douthat (CBS News)
categories: 60Minutes
description: In an interview with 60 Minutes , President Trump said his administration's hardline approach to immigration enforcement around deportations may have been "too tough" in pursuing people in the country for a decade or more. The president spoke with 60 Minutes correspondent Ross Douthat three days after Republicans faced jarring losses in the midterm elections. Support for the party plummeted in South Texas and other heavily Latino areas that trended toward the GOP two years ago — a reversal that many voters linked at least in part to Mr. Trump's immigration crackdown. Mr. Trump said his immigration crackdown "both helped and hurt" him at the polls. He believes he "got an A+ for closing up the border," and got "very high marks for getting the bad ones out."
